Maize Opaque-2 Genomic DNA Sequence

Source: R/data.R
opaque2.Rd

The genomic nucleotide sequence of the maize (Zea mays) opaque endosperm 2 gene, NCBI Gene ID 542375, also known as o2 or Opaque-2. This sequence provides an example of observed categorical data for fitting a Markov chain.

Usage

opaque2

Format

A character vector of length 3,158. Each element is one nucleotide, encoded as "A", "C", "G", or "T", in genomic order. Counts are 798 A, 755 C, 765 G, and 840 T. There are no missing or ambiguous bases.

Source

National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), Gene 542375 and RefSeq NC_050102.1. NCBI places no restrictions on use or distribution of its molecular data; see its data usage policies and disclaimers, including the qualification concerning rights claimed by original submitters.

Details

The source snapshot identifies the gene as LOC542375 on chromosome 7, plus strand, of assembly Zm-B73-REFERENCE-NAM-5.0 (GCF_902167145.1), NCBI Zea mays Annotation Release 103 (2020-08-09). The sequence is the inclusive interval 10,951,530–10,954,687 on RefSeq NC_050102.1. Element \(k\) corresponds to the one-based chromosome coordinate \(10951529 + k\). This is a genomic gene interval, including introns, rather than a spliced transcript or a coding-sequence-only record.

The sequence was taken from the LOC542375.csv file prepared by exe/LOC542375.R in the MarkovExplorer project. The CSV nucleotide column was verified against the accompanying gene.fna; its sequential index column is represented by the vector positions. No bases were removed, reordered, or recoded. The original download date was not recorded; identifiers and coordinates here describe the archived snapshot.

Positions along DNA serve as the sequence index in modelling examples. A first-order, time-homogeneous Markov model is an illustrative assumption, not a verified biological property of these data. This is one sequence, not a collection of independent trajectories for test_const().

See also

fit(), test_prob()

Examples

data(opaque2)
head(opaque2)
#> [1] "A" "A" "T" "C" "C" "A"
table(opaque2)
#> opaque2
#>   A   C   G   T 
#> 798 755 765 840 
fit(opaque2)
#> Markov Chain
#>   Number of states: 4 
#> 
#>   Initial distribution (a):
#>     A T C G 
#>     1 0 0 0 
#> 
#>   Transition matrix (P):
#>               A         T         C         G
#>     A 0.2446675 0.2609787 0.2308657 0.2634881
#>     T 0.2321429 0.2857143 0.2214286 0.2607143
#>     C 0.2860927 0.2860927 0.2264901 0.2013245
#>     G 0.2496732 0.2300654 0.2797386 0.2405229
